reason: Right has a clearer hierarchy with a donut hero, a larger, more legible bar chart with a busiest-month callout, and richer labelled age bars, while Left is correct but plainer and smaller.
Right shows every day as weekday/weekend-coded bars on one zero-based scale with annotations and a tidy comparison, while Left's line chart is thin and its week timeline is awkward.
Left's per-crop scatter plots, best/lowest highlighting and clean table read clearly, whereas Right's heatmap has odd cell seams, and its phone chart drops a county label.

Right uses semantically coloured stacked bars with last-year markers, a clear change chart and numbered actions, while Left's legend colours are illogical (favorable blue, neutral orange, unfavorable green) and its phone layout is clumsy.
Right has a strong headline margin card, a share-of-revenue stacked bar and a large, clearly labelled margin line, while Left is competent but generic.
Right is a polished press release with a navy masthead, gold accents, a tidy fact strip and a contact card, and it adapts well to phone and dark mode.
Right adds a pill nav, icon tiles, numbered claim steps, a callout and a closing CTA, which makes the policy far more scannable than Left's plain bullet lists.
Left has stronger editorial typography, a drop cap, a pull quote and numbered advice cards that break up the long text, while Right is a plain wall of text.
Right visualises the bill split and the tier breakdown with stacked bars and clean ledger cards, though a small clipped label on phone, while Left is just tables.
Left is more designed, but its timeline markers overlap the first letter of every event title on desktop and phone, while Right is plain but clean, aligned and fully readable.
